pageData.heading: Scams that target businesses
pageData.para: Learn the main types of scams your staff should be able to recognise in order to protect your business.

cards.heading: Call first
cards.para: Before you make a first-time payment for any amount you're not prepared to lose, call the payee using a verified phone number to check it’s really them requesting payment.

cards.heading: Set strong, unique passwords
cards.para: Ensure all of your accounts, especially email accounts, have strong, unique passwords and are setup with second-factor authentication (e.g. SMS).

cards.heading: Use an approval process
cards.para: Setup a payments approval process for your business, preferably requiring multiple approvers, with no exceptions.

cards.heading: A culture of questioning
cards.para: Encourage a culture where staff are comfortable to question a payment instruction even if it’s from a senior executive.

cards.heading: Warning Signs
cards.para:
• ⚠️ Unexpected calls claiming you're under investigation.
  • ⚠️Threats of immediate arrest or legal action .
  • ⚠️ Requests for payments via cryptocurrency, gift cards, or wire transfers .
  • ⚠️ Pressure to keep the conversation secret from family or the bank.

cards.heading: What to Do
cards.para:
• ✅ Stay Calm – Real police don’t demand instant payments.
  • ✅ Hang Up & Verify – Call official government or law enforcement numbers.
  • ✅ Never Pay – Authorities never ask for money over the phone.
  • ✅ Report the Scam – Notify law enforcement or cybersecurity agencies.

cards.heading: How Scammers Manipulate Victims
cards.para:
• 🎭 They impersonate police officers, government agencies, or investigators.
  • ⏳ They create a false sense of urgency to stop you from thinking clearly.
  • 🔒 They insist that the matter is confidential and must not be discussed with anyone.
  • 💰 They use fear and intimidation to pressure victims into sending money.

thingsYouShouldKnow.heading: Things You Should Know
paraGraph: DigitalDSA’s Role: DigitalDSA is an independent loan facilitator and web aggregator, connecting users with licensed banks and NBFCs. We do not provide loans directly and do not guarantee approval. All loan terms, conditions, and decisions are solely at the discretion of the respective lender.

Beware of Fraud & Scams: DigitalDSA does not ask for payments, OTPs, or banking credentials at any stage. If you receive such requests claiming to be from DigitalDSA, do not respond and report them immediately.

Fake Loan Offers & Business Email Scams: Scammers may impersonate banks, financial institutions, or DigitalDSA representatives to trick users into making payments or sharing confidential details. Always verify loan offers directly with the lender through official contact details. DigitalDSA is not responsible for financial losses due to third-party fraud.

Remote Access & Digital Arrest Scams: Fraudsters may pretend to be law enforcement or financial regulators, falsely accusing users of financial crimes and demanding payments. DigitalDSA or its partners will never ask for payments through cryptocurrency, gift cards, or wire transfers. If you receive such threats, **hang up and verify through official channels.**

User Responsibility & Security: Users are responsible for verifying the authenticity of any loan-related communication. Protect your personal and financial information by using strong passwords, enabling two-factor authentication, and verifying any payment requests before proceeding. DigitalDSA is not liable for losses due to phishing, scams, or user negligence.

Report Fraud: If you suspect a scam, report it immediately. The Government of India’s **National Cybercrime Helpline (1930)** provides assistance to victims of cyber fraud. Reporting scams early improves the chances of recovery and prevents further fraud.
